{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
[[Category:Shinto Shrines]] [[ja:川原神社]]

The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.

For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.

== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
