{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.

* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

茅輪くぐり }} [[File:Kawaharajinja2.JPG|thumb|250px|right|弁天社]] '''川原神社'''（かわはらじんじゃ）は[[愛知県]][[名古屋市]][[昭和区]]にある神社。[[尾張国]][[愛知郡 (愛知県)|愛智郡]]の[[式内社]]「川原神社」に比定されている。 == 歴史 == 日の神、[[ハニヤス|埴山姫神]]（土の神）、[[ミヅハノメ|罔象女神]]（水の神）を祀っている。防火鎮火の神としても祀られている。建立は定かではないが、[[延喜式]]に初めてその名が出てきている。社殿は[[第二次世界大戦]]で焼失し、再建されたが[[1992年]]（[[平成]]4年）、不慮の火災でまた焼失したため、[[1998年]]（平成10年）に新たに建て直したものである。[[慶長]]6年（[[1601年]]）に[[松平忠吉]]（[[徳川家康]]の四男）が、神領二十石を寄進し、[[寛文]]4年（[[1664年]]）には[[徳川光友]]（[[尾張藩]]2代目藩主）が豊作を祈願している。 == 境内 == 名称は「川原神社」よりも「川名の弁天様」の方がよく通る。[[大正時代]]に小舟が見つかった。これは昔このあたりが入り組んだ海岸線の入り江だったためと言われているからである。毎月3と8のつく日は朝市が開かれ、大勢の人でにぎわう。地元ではしばしば『さんぱち』と呼ばれている。 境内は木々に囲まれ、[[クスノキ]]や[[アラカシ]]などの保存樹も数多く存在する。また、結婚式場としても利用されている。 == 池 == 境内には「弁天池」と呼ばれる池があり、[[弁才天]]が祀られているが神仏分離で近くの曹洞宗太平寺へ遷された。祭神は[[イチキシマヒメ|市杵嶋姫命]]である。また池には[[カメ]]がたくさんいることでも知られ、[[江戸時代]]にかかれた、『[[尾張名所図会]]』にもたくさんのカメが描かれている。たまに民家にカメが現れる事があるが、その時はカメに酒を飲ませてから池に返すのが慣わしとされている。[[2003年]]（平成15年）に崩壊した石垣の修復作業の際、水を抜いたところ357匹ものカメが見つかった。近年は[[ミドリガメ]]が目立ち問題となっていたが多くは駆除され、在来種の[[ニホンイシガメ]]、[[クサガメ]]などが主となっている。 == 末社 == 境内には以下の末社がある。 * 弁天社 * 津島社 * 川名天神社 * [[猿田彦]]社 * 戸隠社 * 秋葉社 * 龍神社 * 川名社 * 川名稲荷社 == 年中行事 == 以下の行事が行われる。 {{Div col}} * 歳旦祭（1月1日） * 鎮火祭（1月17日） * 勧学祭（1月25日） * 初午大祭（旧暦初午） * 弁天祭（4月17日） * 戸隠祭（4月17日） * 津島初祭（6月30日） * 大祓式（6月30日） * 茅の輪、赤丸神事（7月4日） * 津島本祭（7月5日） * 雲霞祭（7月23日） * 川名社祭（9月17日） * 猿田彦社祭（9月17日） * 龍神祭（9月17日） * 川名天神社例祭（9月25日） * 本社試楽祭（10月16日） * 本社例大祭（10月17日） * 七五三祭（11月15日） * 秋葉祭（12月16日） * 大祓式（12月31日） * 本社月次祭（毎月1日・15日） * 川名稲荷社月次祭（毎月8日） {{Div col end}} == 交通アクセス == * [[名古屋市営地下鉄]][[名古屋市営地下鉄鶴舞線|鶴舞線]]「[[川名駅]]」下車、徒歩で約5分。 * [[名古屋市営バス]]「弁天前」バス停下車、目の前。その他「広路通五丁目」「広路小学校」バス停下車。 == 参考文献 == * [[尾張名所図会|『尾張名所図会』 第五巻　川原神社]]、[[1844年]] == 外部リンク == {{osm box|w|548928997}} * [http://www.a-namo.com/ku_info/showaku/hostfo/kawahara/kawao1.html 式内社 川原神社] * {{Wayback|url=http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/owari/bun/ow100707-01.html |title=川原神社 |date=20190101000000}} * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:かわはらしんしや}} [[Category:名古屋市の神社]] [[Category:尾張国の式内社]] [[Category:昭和区の歴史]] [[Category:昭和区の建築物]]

[[江戸期]]まで'''神明'''と呼ばれていたが、[[弁才天]]が祀られていたためしばしば「弁天様」とも呼ばれた。[[飯田街道]]沿いに位置し、江戸初期には既に信仰を集めていた。[[慶長]]6年（[[1601年]]）に[[松平忠吉]]が[[神領]]二十石を[[寄進]]し、[[寛文]]4年（[[1664年]]）には[[徳川光友]]が豊作を祈願したという伝がある。社伝が焼失しているといい、創建年代などに不明な点が多い。当社は[[仏教]]的な側面が強く、[[中世]]には「嶋寺」と呼ばれる[[寺]]があったというが江戸中期には既に荒廃していた。[[天和]]元年（[[1681年]]）に[[黄檗宗]]の[[僧侶]]がこの寺を復興し、弁財天が祀られるようになった。[[神仏分離]]により弁財天は大平寺（[[川名本町]]所在）に移転された。 江戸期に[[天野信景]]が当社を『[[延喜式神名帳]]』に記載のある尾張国愛知郡「川原神社」に比定し、以降定説となった。しかし、天野が当社を川原神社に比定した根拠は所在地が愛知郡川名村で「川」の字が共通している点によるのみであり、[[棟札]]などは残っていない。江戸後期の[[郷土史家]]である[[津田正生]]は当社を「川原神社」に比定することに疑問を呈している。式内社「川原神社」の論社として他に[[鳴海八幡宮]]がある。 社殿は[[第二次世界大戦]]で焼失し、再建されたが[[1992年]]（[[平成]]4年）、不慮の火災でまた焼失したため、[[1998年]]（平成10年）に新たに建て直したものである。 == 境内 == 名称は「川原神社」よりも「川名の弁天様」の方がよく通る。[[大正時代]]に小舟が見つかった。これは昔このあたりが入り組んだ海岸線の入り江だったためと言われているからである。毎月3と8のつく日は朝市が開かれ、大勢の人でにぎわう。地元ではしばしば『さんぱち』と呼ばれている。 境内は木々に囲まれ、[[クスノキ]]や[[アラカシ]]などの保存樹も数多く存在する。また、結婚式場としても利用されている。 == 池 == (日本)|天和]]元年（[[1681年]]）に[[黄檗宗]]の[[僧侶]]がこの寺を復興し、弁財天が祀られるようになった。[[神仏分離]]により弁財天は大平寺（[[川名本町]]所在）に移転された。 江戸期に[[天野信景]]が当社を『[[延喜式神名帳]]』に記載のある尾張国愛知郡「川原神社」に比定し、以降定説となった。しかし、天野が当社を川原神社に比定した根拠は所在地が愛知郡川名村で「川」の字が共通している点によるのみであり、[[棟札]]などは残っていない。江戸後期の[[郷土史家]]である[[津田正生]]は当社を「川原神社」に比定することに疑問を呈している。式内社「川原神社」の論社として他に[[鳴海八幡宮]]がある。 社殿は[[第二次世界大戦]]で焼失し、再建されたが[[1992年]]（[[平成]]4年）、不慮の火災でまた焼失したため、[[1998年]]（平成10年）に新たに建て直したものである。 == 境内 == 名称は「川原神社」よりも「川名の弁天様」の方がよく通る。[[大正時代]]に小舟が見つかった。これは昔このあたりが入り組んだ海岸線の入り江だったためと言われているからである。毎月3と8のつく日は朝市が開かれ、大勢の人でにぎわう。地元ではしばしば『さんぱち』と呼ばれている。 境内は木々に囲まれ、[[クスノキ]]や[[アラカシ]]などの保存樹も数多く存在する。また、結婚式場としても利用されている。 == 池 == 境内には「弁天池」と呼ばれる池があり、[[弁才天]]が祀られているが神仏分離で近くの曹洞宗太平寺へ遷された。祭神は[[イチキシマヒメ|市杵嶋姫命]]である。また池には[[カメ]]がたくさんいることでも知られ、[[江戸時代]]にかかれた、『[[尾張名所図会]]』にもたくさんのカメが描かれている。たまに民家にカメが現れる事があるが、その時はカメに酒を飲ませてから池に返すのが慣わしとされている。[[2003年]]（平成15年）に崩壊した石垣の修復作業の際、水を抜いたところ357匹ものカメが見つかった。近年は[[ミドリガメ]]が目立ち問題となっていたが多くは駆除され、在来種の[[ニホンイシガメ]]、[[クサガメ]]などが主となっている。 津島初祭（6月30日） * 大祓式（6月30日） * 茅の輪、赤丸神事（7月4日） * 津島本祭（7月5日） * 雲霞祭（7月23日） * 川名社祭（9月17日） * 猿田彦社祭（9月17日） * 龍神祭（9月17日） * 川名天神社例祭（9月25日） * 本社試楽祭（10月16日） * 本社例大祭（10月17日） * 七五三祭（11月15日） * 秋葉祭（12月16日） * 大祓式（12月31日） * 本社月次祭（毎月1日・15日） * 川名稲荷社月次祭（毎月8日） {{Div col end}} == 交通アクセス == * [[名古屋市営地下鉄]][[名古屋市営地下鉄鶴舞線|鶴舞線]]「[[川名駅]]」下車、徒歩で約5分。 * [[名古屋市営バス]]「弁天前」バス停下車、目の前。その他「広路通五丁目」「広路小学校」バス停下車。 == 参考文献 == * revision.text:
{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|12=draft}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|12=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|12=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|12=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{otheruses|愛知県名古屋市の神社|三重県伊勢市の神社|川原神社 (伊勢市)}} {{出典の明記|date=2014年9月9日 (火) 11:27 (UTC)}} {{神社 | 画像=[[File:Kawahara-jinja Shrine keidai, Kawana-hommachi Showa Ward Nagoya 2021.jpg|250px]]
境内
（[[2021年]]（[[令和]]3年）5月） | 名称=川原神社 | 所在地=[[愛知県]][[名古屋市]][[昭和区]][[川名本町]]4-4 | 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|9|5.73|N|136|56|40.60|E|region:JP-23_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | 祭神 = 埴山姫神、罔象女神、日神 | 社格 = [[郷社]]→[[県社]]、式内社 | 創建 = 不明（[[17世紀]]以前） | 本殿 = [[神明造]] | 別名 = 神明、川名弁天、川名の弁天様 | 例祭 = [[9月25日]]（川名天神社例祭） | 神事 = 赤丸神事
茅輪くぐり }} [[File:Kawaharajinja2.JPG|thumb|250px|right|弁天社]] '''川原神社'''（かわはらじんじゃ）は[[愛知県]][[名古屋市]][[昭和区]]にある神社。[[尾張国]][[愛知郡 (愛知県)|愛智郡]]の[[式内社]]「川原神社」に比定されている。 == 歴史 == [[江戸期]]まで'''神明'''と呼ばれていたが、[[弁才天]]が祀られていたためしばしば「弁天様」とも呼ばれた。[[飯田街道]]沿いに位置し、江戸初期には既に信仰を集めていた。[[慶長]]6年（[[1601年]]）に[[松平忠吉]]が[[神領]]二十石を[[寄進]]し、[[寛文]]4年（[[1664年]]）には[[徳川光友]]が豊作を祈願したという伝がある。社伝が焼失しているといい、創建年代などに不明な点が多い。当社は[[仏教]]的な側面が強く、[[中世]]には「嶋寺」と呼ばれる[[寺]]があったというが江戸中期には既に荒廃していた。[[天和 (日本)|天和]]元年（[[1681年]]）に[[黄檗宗]]の[[僧侶]]がこの寺を復興し、弁財天が祀られるようになった。[[神仏分離]]により弁財天は大平寺（[[川名本町]]所在）に移転された。 江戸期に[[天野信景]]が当社を『[[延喜式神名帳]]』に記載のある尾張国愛知郡「川原神社」に比定し、以降定説となった。しかし、天野が当社を川原神社に比定した根拠は所在地が愛知郡川名村で「川」の字が共通している点によるのみであり、[[棟札]]などは残っていない。江戸後期の[[郷土史家]]である[[津田正生]]は当社を「川原神社」に比定することに疑問を呈している。式内社「川原神社」の論社として他に[[鳴海八幡宮]]がある。 社殿は[[第二次世界大戦]]で焼失し、再建されたが[[1992年]]（[[平成]]4年）、不慮の火災でまた焼失したため、[[1998年]]（平成10年）に新たに建て直したものである。 == 境内 == 名称は「川原神社」よりも「川名の弁天様」の方がよく通る。[[大正時代]]に小舟が見つかった。これは昔このあたりが入り組んだ海岸線の入り江だったためと言われているからである。毎月3と8のつく日は朝市が開かれ、大勢の人でにぎわう。地元ではしばしば『さんぱち』と呼ばれている。 境内は木々に囲まれ、[[クスノキ]]や[[アラカシ]]などの保存樹も数多く存在する。また、結婚式場としても利用されている。 == 池 == 境内には「弁天池」と呼ばれる池があり、[[弁才天]]が祀られているが神仏分離で近くの曹洞宗太平寺へ遷された。祭神は[[イチキシマヒメ|市杵嶋姫命]]である。また池には[[カメ]]がたくさんいることでも知られ、[[江戸時代]]にかかれた、『[[尾張名所図会]]』にもたくさんのカメが描かれている。たまに民家にカメが現れる事があるが、その時はカメに酒を飲ませてから池に返すのが慣わしとされている。[[2003年]]（平成15年）に崩壊した石垣の修復作業の際、水を抜いたところ357匹ものカメが見つかった。近年は[[ミドリガメ]]が目立ち問題となっていたが多くは駆除され、在来種の[[ニホンイシガメ]]、[[クサガメ]]などが主となっている。 == 末社 == 境内には以下の末社がある。 * 弁天社 * 津島社 * 川名天神社 * [[猿田彦]]社 * 戸隠社 * 秋葉社 * 龍神社 * 川名社 * 川名稲荷社 == 年中行事 == 以下の行事が行われる。 {{Div col}} * 歳旦祭（1月1日） * 鎮火祭（1月17日） * 勧学祭（1月25日） * 初午大祭（旧暦初午） * 弁天祭（4月17日） * 戸隠祭（4月17日） * 津島初祭（6月30日） * 大祓式（6月30日） * 茅の輪、赤丸神事（7月4日） * 津島本祭（7月5日） * 雲霞祭（7月23日） * 川名社祭（9月17日） * 猿田彦社祭（9月17日） * 龍神祭（9月17日） * 川名天神社例祭（9月25日） * 本社試楽祭（10月16日） * 本社例大祭（10月17日） * 七五三祭（11月15日） * 秋葉祭（12月16日） * 大祓式（12月31日） * 本社月次祭（毎月1日・15日） * 川名稲荷社月次祭（毎月8日） {{Div col end}} == 交通アクセス == * [[名古屋市営地下鉄]][[名古屋市営地下鉄鶴舞線|鶴舞線]]「[[川名駅]]」下車、徒歩で約5分。 * [[名古屋市営バス]]「弁天前」バス停下車、目の前。その他「広路通五丁目」「広路小学校」バス停下車。 == 参考文献 == * [[尾張名所図会|『尾張名所図会』 第五巻　川原神社]]、[[1844年]] == 外部リンク == {{osm box|w|548928997}} * [http://www.a-namo.com/ku_info/showaku/hostfo/kawahara/kawao1.html 式内社 川原神社] * {{Wayback|url=http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/owari/bun/ow100707-01.html |title=川原神社 |date=20190101000000}} * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:かわはらしんしや}} [[Category:名古屋市の神社]] {{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
== References ==
{{Reflist|2}}
== 参考文献 == * [[伊勢文化舎]] 編『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、伊勢文化舎、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『日本人なら知っておきたい 伊勢神宮と125の社』タツミムック、[[辰巳出版]]、2013rd year 11月1日、127p. ISBN 978-4-7778-1197-7
