Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. {{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya River (Mie)|qq=}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.

While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya River (Mie)|qq=}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Hinoki|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya River (Mie)|qq=}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.

However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.

Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.

== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

{{Infobox shrine | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|28|6.8|N|136|39|58.7|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = [[Shikinaisha]] (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya River (Mie)|qq=}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya River (Mie)|qq=}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinensai|lt=Kinensai|lt=Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinensai|lt=Kinensai|lt=Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miya River's|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miya River (Mie)|qq=}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, {{ill|Camphor tree|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camphor tree|qq=}}, {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|ja|タブノキ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Machilus thunbergii|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|ja|タラヨウ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ilex latifolia|qq=}}<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamato-hime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinensai|lt=Kinensai|lt=Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinensai|lt=Kinensai|lt=Kinen-sai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinen-sai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niiname-sai|qq=}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-shi Station|qq=}}, served by both {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Central|qq=}} {{ill|Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangū Line|qq=}} and {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}}<ref name="sk5"/>.
