However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.

* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q3194327]] Wikidata name: Kawahara Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:27, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q3194327]] Wikidata name: Kawahara Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:07, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = File:Kawaharajinja1.JPG | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35.15125|N|136.94413889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) | location = {{ill|Kawana-hommachi|qid=Q26160574}} | architecture_style = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545}} }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[:en:学研パブリッシング|学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.

However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. * **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|qq=|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|qq=|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|qq=|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.

However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Kawahara-jinja]][[en:Kawahara Shrine]][[fr:Kawahara-jinja]][[ja:川原神社]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q3194327]] Wikidata name: Kawahara Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:27, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q3194327]] Wikidata name: Kawahara Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:07, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building | Name = Kawara Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = File:Kawaharajinja1.JPG | location = Izumi 1559, Saha-cho, [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35.15125|N|136.94413889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Map = Japan Mie | deity = [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] | type = {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor Rank), {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) | Established = Before 927 CE (Enchō 5) | Main Hall = [[Shinmei-zukuri]] | Other Names = | festival = | Rituals = [[Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]] (Harvest Festival) | location = {{ill|Kawana-hommachi|WD=Q26160574}} | architecture_style = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545}} }}
'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.

* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. '''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]], Japan.
== Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.
This shrine was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]], with its enshrined deity considered the [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miya River's]] [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.
It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk"/>. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.
The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.
== Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic"/>. The forest includes species such as [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Camphor tree]], {{ill|Oak|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|1=Cyclobalanopsis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q796117}}, [[:en:Machilus thunbergii|Machilus thunbergii]], and [[:en:Ilex latifolia|Ilex latifolia]]<ref name="sk7"/>.
== Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm"/>. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.
Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}<ref name="sk6"/>.
== History == According to legend, [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic"/>. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]] and [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm"/>. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk6"/>.
In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk5"/>. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk5"/>. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk6"/>. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae<ref name="tm"/>.
Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk5"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Rituals == During the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinen-sai]], {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]], [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niiname-sai]], and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk6"/>. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk6"/>.
== Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.
* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic"/>. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|1=Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise-shi Station]], served by both [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR Central]] [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangū Line]] and [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]] [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]]<ref name="sk5"/>.
