{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|1=Kōtai Jingū}} auxiliary shrine |Established = Before the 5th year of {{ill|lt=Enchō (era)|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|qid=Q30470|1=927}}) |Main hall style = {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} |Other names = |Pilgrimage designation = |Annual festival = |Rituals = {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}} |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|label=Kawara Shrine|position=bottom|width=180|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=180|frame-height=200}} }} '''Kawara Shrine''' (かわらじんじゃ) is an {{ill|lt=auxiliary shrine|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha|1=Setsumatsusha}} of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|1=Kōtai Jingū}} (Inner Shrine). === Overview === It ranks 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp. 9–11 It is a {{ill|lt=shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} designated by {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, and the {{ill|lt=enshrined deity|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|1=Saijin}} is said to be the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957|1=Guardian deities}} of the {{ill|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|Q6884164|qid=Q6884164|1=Miya River (Mie)}}.Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 70Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 71 The shrine is located on the east bank of the Miyagawa River, at 1559 Sensui, aza Sōchi, Sōchi-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|qid=Q328067|1=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196|1=Mie Prefecture}}.Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 76 The place name “Sōchi” means “marshland,” indicating that wetlands from the Miyagawa once existed there. There are also records stating that rice was offered from Sōchi to the Inner Shrine.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 346 The shrine name appears as “Kawara Shrine” in the *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō*, while other sources list it as “Kawara Shrine” or “Kawara-sha.” Records state that local residents referred to it as “Senzui” (river water, spring water), “Odago,” or “Yagura.”Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 345 === Precincts === The shrine grounds cover an {{ill|lt=area|Q11500|qid=Q11500|1=Area}} of 3,219 {{ill|lt=square meters|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m2|1=Square metre}}.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 347 The {{ill|lt=precincts|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002|1=keidai}} form a tranquil space filled with dappled sunlight, birdsong, and the murmur of the river. Trees such as {{ill|lt=Japanese cypress|Q917187|qid=Q917187|1=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|lt=camphor tree|Q158722|qid=Q158722|1=Camphora officinarum}}, {{ill|lt=oak|Q796117|qid=Q796117|1=Cyclobalanopsis}}, {{ill|lt=Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073|1=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|lt=Ilex latifolia|Q2706373|qid=Q2706373|1=Ilex latifolia}} grow densely within the grounds. === Enshrined deity === The enshrined deity is {{ill|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. This is the same {{ill|lt=deity (Shinto)|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=kami|1=Kami}} worshipped at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Yoru-no-miya)|Q11516023|qid=Q11516023|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)}}, among the 125 shrines of Ise Grand Shrine. While Tsukuyomi is generally regarded as a {{ill|lt=moon|Q405|qid=Q405|1=Moon}} deity, the moon and {{ill|lt=water|Q283|qid=Q283|1=Water}} are considered closely related, and in the context of Kawara Shrine, Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama is regarded as a river deity. In addition to sharing the same enshrined deity, there is a theory that Sōchi-chō, where Kawara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-chō, where Tsukiyomi Shrine is located, were both deeply connected through the {{ill|lt=Arakida clan|Q11618716|qid=Q11618716|1=Arakida clan}}. === History === According to tradition, {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was welcomed here by Ōwakako-no-Mikoto and traveled down the Miyagawa River by boat. Regarding its establishment, based on the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, it is believed to have been founded before the compilation of the *{{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}*, that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|lt=Enchō (era)|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|qid=Q30470|1=927}}).Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 22 According to the *Daijingū-shiki*, it was designated as one of the shrines involved in repairs by the {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}, and it received offerings during the Kinensai and Kannamesai festivals. However, during the {{ill|lt=Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period|1=Sengoku period}}, {{ill|lt=rituals|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}} were discontinued, and the shrine grounds fell into ruin. The hereditary priests ({{ill|lt=hafuri|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|lt=hafuri|1=Gūji}}) who had been appointed until then also died out. In the 3rd year of {{ill|lt=Kanbun|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228|1=Kanbun (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577|1=1663}}), {{ill|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|Q92924151|qid=Q92924151|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|1=Kiyonaga Kawabe}} restored the shrine at Sōchi. On the 9th day of the 9th month (lunar calendar; {{ill|lt=Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138|1=Gregorian calendar}}: {{ill|lt=October 9|Q2923|qid=Q2923|1=October 9}}, 1663), the {{ill|lt=shrine buildings|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}} were constructed, and on the 12th day of the 12th month (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=January 10|Q2243|qid=Q2243|1=January 10}}, {{ill|lt=1664|Q7581|qid=Q7581|1=1664}}), the deity was ceremonially transferred ({{ill|lt=sengu|Q24892914|qid=Q24892914|1=Sengyo}}). At that time, families that had formerly served as hereditary priests were sought out and reinstated. During the restoration, local traditions and place names were referenced, but there is also a theory that Takehana Shrine in present-day Takegahana-chō, Ise City, or {{ill|lt=Kawarabuchi Shrine|Q17209232|qid=Q17209232|1=Kawarabuchi Shrine}} in {{ill|lt=Fun'e (Ise City)|Q17213313|qid=Q17213313|1=Funae}} may have been the original site. Since a subsequent deity transfer on the 29th day of the 3rd month of the 7th year of {{ill|lt=Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001|1=Genroku}} (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=April 23|Q2527|qid=Q2527|1=April 23}}, {{ill|lt=1694|Q7694|qid=Q7694|1=1694}}), the shrine site has not moved. The shrine buildings were rebuilt in November {{ill|lt=1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056|1=1908}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 41).Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): p. 11 They were subsequently rebuilt again in May {{ill|lt=1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754|1=1960}} ({{ill|lt=Shōwa|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}} 35), and repairs were carried out in September {{ill|lt=1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434|1=1983}} (Shōwa 58). === Rituals === During the Kinensai, {{ill|lt=Tsukinamisai|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, and extraordinary festivals, {{ill|lt=Shinto priests|Q60523|qid=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} present {{ill|lt=offerings|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=shinsen|1=Shinsen}} and {{ill|lt=heihaku|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885|1=Hanpei}} before the shrine. For rites such as the {{ill|lt=Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}}, remote worship is performed at the Inner Shrine’s Gojōden Hall. === Access === The shrine is situated in a forest slightly off {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 22 (Ise–Minamishima Line)|Q11357908|qid=Q11357908|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22}}.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp. 346–347 * About a 12-minute walk (700 {{ill|lt=meters|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m|1=Metre}}) from the “Sōchi” {{ill|lt=bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806|1=Bus stop}} on a {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516|1=Mie Kotsu}} {{ill|lt=route bus|Q1373492|qid=Q1373492|1=Transit bus}}. Enter the alley opposite {{ill|lt=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School|Q11379036|qid=Q11379036|1=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School}} near the bus stop and follow the rice paddies to reach the precincts. * Approximately 5.5 {{ill|lt=kilometers|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km|1=Kilometre}} from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|qid=Q6079748|1=Iseshi Station}} on the {{ill|lt=JR Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023|1=Sangū Line}} of {{ill|lt=Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679|1=Central Japan Railway Company}} or the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line|Q900630|qid=Q900630|1=Yamada Line (Kintetsu)}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085|1=Kintetsu Railway}}. === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist|2}} === References === * {{ill|lt=Ise ed., *History of Ujiyamada City, Vol. 1*, Ujiyamada City Office, January 20, 1929, 862 pp. * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gakken Publishing|1=UNKNOWN}} ed., *Let’s Go to Ise Grand Shrine*, Gakken Mook Shrine translation== '''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. == Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11. This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miya River's|1=Miya River (Mie)}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71. It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie PrefectureTatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from SochiShikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346. The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345. == Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|en|Chamaecyparis obtusa|qid=Q917187|lt=Chamaecyparis obtusa|1=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=Camphor tree|1=Camphora officinarum}}, {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q796117|1=Cyclobalanopsis}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|en|Machilus thunbergii|qid=Q5792073|lt=Machilus thunbergii|1=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|en|Ilex latifolia|qid=Q2706373|lt=Ilex latifolia|1=Ilex latifolia}}. == Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂). This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|ja|月夜見宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine. Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}. == History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of IseIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.22. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai|1=Kinensai}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}. However, during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared. In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae. Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58). == Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai|1=Kinensai}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine. == Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357908|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22}}Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347. * **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kōtsū|1=Mie Kotsu}} "Sochi" bus stop. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379036|1=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station|1=Iseshi Station}}, served by both {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central|1=Central Japan Railway Company}} {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line|1=Sangū Line}} and {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|en|Kintetsu Railway|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu|1=Kintetsu Railway}} {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line|1=Yamada Line (Kintetsu)}}. == References == == Bibliography == * [[伊勢文化舎]] 編『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、伊勢文化舎、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[:en:学研パブリッシング|学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『日本人なら知っておきたい 伊勢神宮と125の社』タツミムック、[[辰巳出版]]、2013rd year 11月1日、127p. ISBN 978-4-7778-1197-7 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=}} * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|qq=}} * [[河原神社 (伊勢市)]] - 伊勢神宮{{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|zh|豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}（外宮）摂社。 * [[宮本村 (三重県)]] == External Links == {{external media|align=|width=230px|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image1=[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/images/shrine/area05/area05_02.jpg 川原神社]}} * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m06/0607.html 川原神社（かわらじんじゃ）] - 一般財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{125 Shrines of Ise}} == Japanese content == {{Shrine |Name = Kawara Shrine |Image = [[File:Kawara-jinja (Naiku) 01.jpg|250px]] |Location = {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196|1=Mie Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|qid=Q328067|1=Ise, Mie}} Sōchi-chō {{ill|lt=Koaza|Q5327509|qid=Q5327509|lt=aza|1=koaza}} Sensui 1559 |Coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} |Enshrined deity = {{ill|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}} |Shrine rank = {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (minor)
{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|1=Kōtai Jingū}} auxiliary shrine |Established = Before the 5th year of {{ill|lt=Enchō (era)|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|qid=Q30470|1=927}}) |Main hall style = {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} |Other names = |Pilgrimage designation = |Annual festival = |Rituals = {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}} |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|label=Kawara Shrine|position=bottom|width=180|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=180|frame-height=200}} }} '''Kawara Shrine''' (かわらじんじゃ) is an {{ill|lt=auxiliary shrine|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha|1=Setsumatsusha}} of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|1=Kōtai Jingū}} (Inner Shrine). === Overview === It ranks 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp. 9–11 It is a {{ill|lt=shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} designated by {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, and the {{ill|lt=enshrined deity|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|1=Saijin}} is said to be the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957|1=Guardian deities}} of the {{ill|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|Q6884164|qid=Q6884164|1=Miya River (Mie)}}.Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 70Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 71 The shrine is located on the east bank of the Miyagawa River, at 1559 Sensui, aza Sōchi, Sōchi-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|qid=Q328067|1=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196|1=Mie Prefecture}}.Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 76 The place name “Sōchi” means “marshland,” indicating that wetlands from the Miyagawa once existed there. There are also records stating that rice was offered from Sōchi to the Inner Shrine.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 346 The shrine name appears as “Kawara Shrine” in the *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō*, while other sources list it as “Kawara Shrine” or “Kawara-sha.” Records state that local residents referred to it as “Senzui” (river water, spring water), “Odago,” or “Yagura.”Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 345 === Precincts === The shrine grounds cover an {{ill|lt=area|Q11500|qid=Q11500|1=Area}} of 3,219 {{ill|lt=square meters|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m2|1=Square metre}}.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 347 The {{ill|lt=precincts|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002|1=keidai}} form a tranquil space filled with dappled sunlight, birdsong, and the murmur of the river. Trees such as {{ill|lt=Japanese cypress|Q917187|qid=Q917187|1=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|lt=camphor tree|Q158722|qid=Q158722|1=Camphora officinarum}}, {{ill|lt=oak|Q796117|qid=Q796117|1=Cyclobalanopsis}}, {{ill|lt=Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073|1=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|lt=Ilex latifolia|Q2706373|qid=Q2706373|1=Ilex latifolia}} grow densely within the grounds. === Enshrined deity === The enshrined deity is {{ill|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. This is the same {{ill|lt=deity (Shinto)|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=kami|1=Kami}} worshipped at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Yoru-no-miya)|Q11516023|qid=Q11516023|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)}}, among the 125 shrines of Ise Grand Shrine. While Tsukuyomi is generally regarded as a {{ill|lt=moon|Q405|qid=Q405|1=Moon}} deity, the moon and {{ill|lt=water|Q283|qid=Q283|1=Water}} are considered closely related, and in the context of Kawara Shrine, Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama is regarded as a river deity. In addition to sharing the same enshrined deity, there is a theory that Sōchi-chō, where Kawara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-chō, where Tsukiyomi Shrine is located, were both deeply connected through the {{ill|lt=Arakida clan|Q11618716|qid=Q11618716|1=Arakida clan}}. === History === According to tradition, {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was welcomed here by Ōwakako-no-Mikoto and traveled down the Miyagawa River by boat. Regarding its establishment, based on the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, it is believed to have been founded before the compilation of the *{{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}*, that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|lt=Enchō (era)|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|qid=Q30470|1=927}}).Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 22 According to the *Daijingū-shiki*, it was designated as one of the shrines involved in repairs by the {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}, and it received offerings during the Kinensai and Kannamesai festivals. However, during the {{ill|lt=Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period|1=Sengoku period}}, {{ill|lt=rituals|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}} were discontinued, and the shrine grounds fell into ruin. The hereditary priests ({{ill|lt=hafuri|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|lt=hafuri|1=Gūji}}) who had been appointed until then also died out. In the 3rd year of {{ill|lt=Kanbun|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228|1=Kanbun (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577|1=1663}}), {{ill|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|Q92924151|qid=Q92924151|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|1=Kiyonaga Kawabe}} restored the shrine at Sōchi. On the 9th day of the 9th month (lunar calendar; {{ill|lt=Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138|1=Gregorian calendar}}: {{ill|lt=October 9|Q2923|qid=Q2923|1=October 9}}, 1663), the {{ill|lt=shrine buildings|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}} were constructed, and on the 12th day of the 12th month (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=January 10|Q2243|qid=Q2243|1=January 10}}, {{ill|lt=1664|Q7581|qid=Q7581|1=1664}}), the deity was ceremonially transferred ({{ill|lt=sengu|Q24892914|qid=Q24892914|1=Sengyo}}). At that time, families that had formerly served as hereditary priests were sought out and reinstated. During the restoration, local traditions and place names were referenced, but there is also a theory that Takehana Shrine in present-day Takegahana-chō, Ise City, or {{ill|lt=Kawarabuchi Shrine|Q17209232|qid=Q17209232|1=Kawarabuchi Shrine}} in {{ill|lt=Fun'e (Ise City)|Q17213313|qid=Q17213313|1=Funae}} may have been the original site. Since a subsequent deity transfer on the 29th day of the 3rd month of the 7th year of {{ill|lt=Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001|1=Genroku}} (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=April 23|Q2527|qid=Q2527|1=April 23}}, {{ill|lt=1694|Q7694|qid=Q7694|1=1694}}), the shrine site has not moved. The shrine buildings were rebuilt in November {{ill|lt=1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056|1=1908}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 41).Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): p. 11 They were subsequently rebuilt again in May {{ill|lt=1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754|1=1960}} ({{ill|lt=Shōwa|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}} 35), and repairs were carried out in September {{ill|lt=1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434|1=1983}} (Shōwa 58). === Rituals === During the Kinensai, {{ill|lt=Tsukinamisai|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, and extraordinary festivals, {{ill|lt=Shinto priests|Q60523|qid=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} present {{ill|lt=offerings|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=shinsen|1=Shinsen}} and {{ill|lt=heihaku|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885|1=Hanpei}} before the shrine. For rites such as the {{ill|lt=Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}}, remote worship is performed at the Inner Shrine’s Gojōden Hall. === Access === The shrine is situated in a forest slightly off {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 22 (Ise–Minamishima Line)|Q11357908|qid=Q11357908|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22}}.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp. 346–347 * About a 12-minute walk (700 {{ill|lt=meters|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m|1=Metre}}) from the “Sōchi” {{ill|lt=bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806|1=Bus stop}} on a {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516|1=Mie Kotsu}} {{ill|lt=route bus|Q1373492|qid=Q1373492|1=Transit bus}}. Enter the alley opposite {{ill|lt=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School|Q11379036|qid=Q11379036|1=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School}} near the bus stop and follow the rice paddies to reach the precincts. * Approximately 5.5 {{ill|lt=kilometers|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km|1=Kilometre}} from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|qid=Q6079748|1=Iseshi Station}} on the {{ill|lt=JR Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023|1=Sangū Line}} of {{ill|lt=Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679|1=Central Japan Railway Company}} or the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line|Q900630|qid=Q900630|1=Yamada Line (Kintetsu)}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085|1=Kintetsu Railway}}. === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist|2}} === References === * {{ill|lt=Ise Bunka-sha|Q11379080|qid=Q11379080|1=Ise Bunka-sha}}, ed., *Oise-san 125-sha Meguri*, supplement *Isebito*, Ise Bunka-sha, December 23, 2008, 151 pp. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 * Ujiyamada City Office, ed., *History of Ujiyamada City, Vol. 1*, Ujiyamada City Office, January 20, 1929, 862 pp. * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gakken Publishing|1=UNKNOWN}} ed., *Let’s Go to Ise Grand Shrine*, Gakken Mook Shrine Association, ed., *Shikinaisha Survey Report, Vol. 6: Tōkaidō 1*, {{ill|lt=Kōgakkan University|Q1797584|qid=Q1797584|1=Kogakkan University}} Press, February 28, 1990, 690 pp. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * *Ise translation== '''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. == Overview == Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine)Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11. This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miya River's|1=Miya River (Mie)}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71. It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie PrefectureTatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from SochiShikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346. The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345. == Grounds == The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|en|Chamaecyparis obtusa|qid=Q917187|lt=Chamaecyparis obtusa|1=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=Camphor tree|1=Camphora officinarum}}, {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q796117|1=Cyclobalanopsis}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|en|Machilus thunbergii|qid=Q5792073|lt=Machilus thunbergii|1=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|en|Ilex latifolia|qid=Q2706373|lt=Ilex latifolia|1=Ilex latifolia}}. == Enshrined deity == The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂). This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|ja|月夜見宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya|qq=|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine. Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakida clan|qq=}}. == History == According to legend, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of IseIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.22. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai|1=Kinensai}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}. However, during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared. In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine in Sochi. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takegahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}} in Funae. Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58). == Rituals == During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai|1=Kinensai}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the Inner Shrine. == Access == The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357908|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22}}Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347. * **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kōtsū|1=Mie Kotsu}} "Sochi" bus stop. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379036|1=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine. * **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station|1=Iseshi Station}}, served by both {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central|1=Central Japan Railway Company}} {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line|1=Sangū Line}} and {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|en|Kintetsu Railway|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu|1=Kintetsu Railway}} {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line|1=Yamada Line (Kintetsu)}}. == References == == Bibliography == * [[伊勢文化舎]] 編『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、伊勢文化舎、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. (1929): pp. 9–11 It is a {{ill|lt=shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} designated by {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, and the {{ill|lt=enshrined deity|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|1=Saijin}} is said to be the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957|1=Guardian deities}} of the {{ill|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|Q6884164|qid=Q6884164|1=Miya River (Mie)}}.Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 70Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 71 The shrine is located on the east bank of the Miyagawa River, at 1559 Sensui, aza Sōchi, Sōchi-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|qid=Q328067|1=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196|1=Mie Prefecture}}.Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 76 The place name “Sōchi” means “marshland,” indicating that wetlands from the Miyagawa once existed there. There are also records stating that rice was offered from Sōchi to the Inner Shrine.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 346 The shrine name appears as “Kawara Shrine” in the *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō*, while other sources list it as “Kawara Shrine” or “Kawara-sha.” Records state that local residents referred to it as “Senzui” (river water, spring water), “Odago,” or “Yagura.”Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 345 === Precincts === The shrine grounds cover an {{ill|lt=area|Q11500|qid=Q11500|1=Area}} of 3,219 {{ill|lt=square meters|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m2|1=Square metre}}.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 347 The {{ill|lt=precincts|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002|1=keidai}} form a tranquil space filled with dappled sunlight, birdsong, and the murmur of the river. Trees such as {{ill|lt=Japanese cypress|Q917187|qid=Q917187|1=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|lt=camphor tree|Q158722|qid=Q158722|1=Camphora officinarum}}, {{ill|lt=oak|Q796117|qid=Q796117|1=Cyclobalanopsis}}, {{ill|lt=Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073|1=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|lt=Ilex latifolia|Q2706373|qid=Q2706373|1=Ilex latifolia}} grow densely within the grounds. === Enshrined deity === The enshrined deity is {{ill|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. This is the same {{ill|lt=deity (Shinto)|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=kami|1=Kami}} worshipped at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Yoru-no-miya)|Q11516023|qid=Q11516023|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)}}, among the 125 shrines of Ise Grand Shrine. While Tsukuyomi is generally regarded as a {{ill|lt=moon|Q405|qid=Q405|1=Moon}} deity, the moon and {{ill|lt=water|Q283|qid=Q283|1=Water}} are considered closely related, and in the context of Kawara Shrine, Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama is regarded as a river deity. In addition to sharing the same enshrined deity, there is a theory that Sōchi-chō, where Kawara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-chō, where Tsukiyomi Shrine is located, were both deeply connected through the {{ill|lt=Arakida clan|Q11618716|qid=Q11618716|1=Arakida clan}}. === History === According to tradition, {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was welcomed here by Ōwakako-no-Mikoto and traveled down the Miyagawa River by boat. Regarding its establishment, based on the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, it is believed to have been founded before the compilation of the *{{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}*, that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|lt=Enchō (era)|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|qid=Q30470|1=927}}).Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 22 According to the *Daijingū-shiki*, it was designated as one of the shrines involved in repairs by the {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}, and it received offerings during the Kinensai and Kannamesai festivals. However, during the {{ill|lt=Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period|1=Sengoku period}}, {{ill|lt=rituals|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}} were discontinued, and the shrine grounds fell into ruin. The hereditary priests ({{ill|lt=hafuri|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|lt=hafuri|1=Gūji}}) who had been appointed until then also died out. In the 3rd year of {{ill|lt=Kanbun|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228|1=Kanbun (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577|1=1663}}), {{ill|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|Q92924151|qid=Q92924151|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|1=Kiyonaga Kawabe}} restored the shrine at Sōchi. On the 9th day of the 9th month (lunar calendar; {{ill|lt=Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138|1=Gregorian calendar}}: {{ill|lt=October 9|Q2923|qid=Q2923|1=October 9}}, 1663), the {{ill|lt=shrine buildings|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}} were constructed, and on the 12th day of the 12th month (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=January 10|Q2243|qid=Q2243|1=January 10}}, {{ill|lt=1664|Q7581|qid=Q7581|1=1664}}), the deity was ceremonially transferred ({{ill|lt=sengu|Q24892914|qid=Q24892914|1=Sengyo}}). At that time, families that had formerly served as hereditary priests were sought out and reinstated. During the restoration, local traditions and place names were referenced, but there is also a theory that Takehana Shrine in present-day Takegahana-chō, Ise City, or {{ill|lt=Kawarabuchi Shrine|Q17209232|qid=Q17209232|1=Kawarabuchi Shrine}} in {{ill|lt=Fun'e (Ise City)|Q17213313|qid=Q17213313|1=Funae}} may have been the original site. Since a subsequent deity transfer on the 29th day of the 3rd month of the 7th year of {{ill|lt=Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001|1=Genroku}} (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=April 23|Q2527|qid=Q2527|1=April 23}}, {{ill|lt=1694|Q7694|qid=Q7694|1=1694}}), the shrine site has not moved. The shrine buildings were rebuilt in November {{ill|lt=1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056|1=1908}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 41).Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): p. 11 They were subsequently rebuilt again in May {{ill|lt=1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754|1=1960}} ({{ill|lt=Shōwa|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}} 35), and repairs were carried out in September {{ill|lt=1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434|1=1983}} (Shōwa 58). === Rituals === During the Kinensai, {{ill|lt=Tsukinamisai|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, and extraordinary festivals, {{ill|lt=Shinto priests|Q60523|qid=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} present {{ill|lt=offerings|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=shinsen|1=Shinsen}} and {{ill|lt=heihaku|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885|1=Hanpei}} before the shrine. For rites such as the {{ill|lt=Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}}, remote worship is performed at the Inner Shrine’s Gojōden Hall. === Access === The shrine is situated in a forest slightly off {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 22 (Ise–Minamishima Line)|Q11357908|qid=Q11357908|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22}}.Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp. 346–347 * About a 12-minute walk (700 {{ill|lt=meters|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m|1=Metre}}) from the “Sōchi” {{ill|lt=bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806|1=Bus stop}} on a {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516|1=Mie Kotsu}} {{ill|lt=route bus|Q1373492|qid=Q1373492|1=Transit bus}}. Enter the alley opposite {{ill|lt=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School|Q11379036|qid=Q11379036|1=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School}} near the bus stop and follow the rice paddies to reach the precincts. * Approximately 5.5 {{ill|lt=kilometers|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km|1=Kilometre}} from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|qid=Q6079748|1=Iseshi Station}} on the {{ill|lt=JR Sangū
